text:
Marathon Petroleum stock fell 3.9% today, extending a sharp two-week decline of 18%, as oil prices pulled back Friday following the midterm elections. The pullback reflects investor uncertainty about geopolitical risk—while some analysts warn that renewed U.S.-Iran tensions could push oil higher, markets are currently pricing in caution rather than escalation, weighing on refiner margins when crude becomes cheaper relative to refined products. Oil storage levels remain elevated (692 million barrels), which can also pressure refiner profitability when inventory builds.

The stock's decline tracks a broader shift in sentiment since the company reported quarterly earnings on November 3rd. A Democratic-controlled Congress is seen as more favorable to renewable energy expansion, which doesn't directly hurt refining but reflects a longer-term headwind for traditional oil refiners as energy policy shifts away from fossil fuels.
